investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict) — Eval Failure on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T06:45:09–13Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the inner error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every sibling check's probe path, the quota rejection prevented any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the org used by the observability probe account has reached the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because createAgent() is called at the very start of each remote-agents probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1859), the 409 is the earliest violated boundary and prevents all downstream evidence collection. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely: the probe org account has accumulated 100 or more swarm agents (from prior eval runs, leaked cleanup, or other usage) and the swarm service is enforcing a hard per-org limit of 100, blocking any new agent creation.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: POST /api/agents blocked by swarm agent quota (HTTP 409, limit 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T06:45:11–13Z with the identical 409 conflict response: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval runner calls createAgent() as its first step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1879), and that call is being rejected by the swarm backend before any agent identity or state evidence can be collected, causing every required evidence field (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to remain missing.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 for the eval's org and is returning HTTP 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents attempt. Because createAgent() is the prerequisite step for all three remote-agents checks, none of them can proceed past agent creation, and no evidence is written. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint: the eval probe org has reached or exceeded the swarm agent quota, preventing new agent creation. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this cannot be characterized as a user-facing outage.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit 100)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-06-19T06:45:11–13Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents, indicating the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-scoped remote agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation was blocked at the API boundary, no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. The eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1892) calls createAgent as its first substantive step; because that call was rejected before any agent was provisioned, the probe could not proceed to collect any of the five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266–269. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition on the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict) — Eval Failure on POST /api/agents
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T06:45:09–13Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents, carrying the inner error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the agent creation call is the first step in every sibling check's probe path, the quota rejection prevented any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected, causing a complete contract gap for the remote-agent-create eval.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the org used by the observability probe account has reached the 100-agent hard limit enforced by the swarm service. Because createAgent() is called at the very start of each remote-agents probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1859), the 409 is the earliest violated boundary and prevents all downstream evidence collection. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely: the probe org account has accumulated 100 or more swarm agents (from prior eval runs, leaked cleanup, or other usage) and the swarm service is enforcing a hard per-org limit of 100, blocking any new agent creation.
Possible: a previous eval run's withCleanup() teardown failed to delete one or more remote agents, causing agents to accumulate over time until the quota was reached.
Possible: the quota limit of 100 was recently lowered on the swarm service side, causing an org that was previously under the limit to now be over it.
Less likely: the probe org is shared with non-eval workloads that independently consumed agent quota, pushing the count to the limit.

investigations.title: Remote Agents eval failure: POST /api/agents blocked by swarm agent quota (HTTP 409, limit 100)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-19T06:45:11–13Z with the identical 409 conflict response: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval runner calls createAgent() as its first step (run-status-probes.mjs line 1879), and that call is being rejected by the swarm backend before any agent identity or state evidence can be collected, causing every required evidence field (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to remain missing.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend is enforcing a hard agent quota of 100 for the eval's org and is returning HTTP 409 "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents attempt. Because createAgent() is the prerequisite step for all three remote-agents checks, none of them can proceed past agent creation, and no evidence is written. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint: the eval probe org has reached or exceeded the swarm agent quota, preventing new agent creation. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so this cannot be characterized as a user-facing outage.

Tertiary — a cleanup race condition or crash in a prior eval run left orphaned agents in the eval org, consuming quota slots without being released, and the cumulative count has now reached 100.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-06-19T06:45:11–13Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents, indicating the swarm backend rejected agent creation because the org-scoped remote agent quota of 100 has been reached. Because agent creation was blocked at the API boundary, no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. The eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1892) calls createAgent as its first substantive step; because that call was rejected before any agent was provisioned, the probe could not proceed to collect any of the five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266–269. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition on the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence.

Less likely: The eval runner is being executed concurrently by multiple workflows, each creating agents without waiting for cleanup, collectively exceeding the quota within a single run window.
